title: Fairness in AI-Driven Recruitment: Challenges, Metrics, Methods, and Future Directions

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic review of existing literature and case studies evaluating gender disparities in AI-driven job ad targeting, resume screening tools (e.g., penalizing female-associated words), and language models perpetuating gender stereotypes.

Synthesis of prior research highlighting racial disparities and stereotyping in job advertisement delivery algorithms, resume scoring using large language models, and facial/speech analysis in automated video interviews.

Reviewing empirical studies on automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems used in automated hiring interviews that demonstrate significant accuracy disparities and penalties for individuals with speech disabilities, such as stuttering or dysarthria.
Analysis of literature assessing automated interview transcription and scoring systems, noting performance degradation and accuracy disparities for non-native English speakers.
Reviewing literature on automated job advertisement generation and sourcing, identifying how biased textual language and keyword usage can perpetuate age-related stereotypes and deter applicants.
Examination of prior studies demonstrating that foundational large language models encode prejudices against certain religious groups, which can propagate into downstream candidate evaluation tasks.
